Action Plan:
1. Send electronic prescription for a 3-day course of oral antibiotics for presumed uncomplicated UTI to Knightsbridge pharmacy; patient to collect within the hour.  
2. Encourage oral hydration 2.5–3 L water/day; consider cranberry juice and OTC urinary alkalinising sachets (details to be provided in notes).  
3. Patient to purchase a thermometer and monitor temperature at home.  
4. Safety-net: return urgently if pain worsens, develops lower-back/loin pain, fever, difficulty passing urine, or if symptoms persist/recur after antibiotics.  
5. No routine follow-up required if symptoms resolve; seek review if no improvement after completing antibiotics or for recurrent episodes.  
6. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint: Painful urination for 6 days.  
• HPI:  
  – Dysuria with foul-smelling urine.  
  – Intermittent mid-lower abdominal pain, 7/10, comes and goes.  
  – Small spots of blood in urine.  
  – Able to pass urine; no fever reported; no loin/back pain; eating/drinking normally; no vaginal discharge.  
  – No previous similar episodes.  
• Past medical history: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). No prior UTIs or kidney problems. No surgeries.  
• Medications: Mebeverine 200 mg three times daily.  
• Allergies: Clindamycin (reaction not specified).  
• Social history: Lives with friends; support worker. Alcohol: ~1 glass wine/week. Non-smoker.  
• Family history: Non-contributory.

Objective:
• No physical examination or vital signs recorded during teleconsultation.  
• No investigations performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Dysuria with hematuria  
   - Assessment: Acute uncomplicated urinary tract infection (cystitis).  
   - Differential: Urethritis, vaginitis, renal/ureteric calculi, interstitial cystitis.  
   - Investigations: None at present; urine culture if symptoms persist or recur.  
   - Treatment: 3-day course oral antibiotics (drug/dose/route/frequency not documented); advise increased fluids, cranberry juice, urinary alkalinising sachets.  
   - Referrals: None.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing expected elements: vital signs, physical abdominal/renal exam findings, antibiotic name/dose/route/frequency, reaction details for Clindamycin allergy.  
• No internal transcript conflicts noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor inaudible words did not affect clinical content.
